# ADR-0021: Event Values generated by a SoundToGlobalController

Status: Accepted (owner decision 2026-10-03)

## Context

A SoundToGlobalController takes a number, a pasted Sound, or an Event
expression as its input and generates a corresponding Event Value, which
every other Sound sees as it sees Event Values from the Virtual Control
Surface or an external MIDI source. A GeneratedEvent of `!Wobble` lets every other field that
reads `!Wobble` follow the Value. The Virtual Control Surface maps the Value
as it maps a fader, from its minimum to its maximum.

Ours could only be the project's single terminal, recording the Value as
timed events for the host, so a generated Event Value reached no Sound and
the Sound that used it could not be played at the same time.

Passing generated events through the runtime's Event Value store would make
them take effect a block or a callback later, and offline blocks and
realtime callbacks do not partition alike, so the two renderers would
disagree.

## Decision

A SoundToGlobalController generates its Event Value when it is not the
project's only terminal. The generated name is resolved when the project
is compiled: every expression field of the project, in its graph and its
Sound definitions, that reads the generated Event Value reads the
controller's Value instead.

- A Value written in the Value field is substituted, in parentheses, for
  the Event Value reference.
- A Value fed by a Sound connected to the controller's `value` input makes
  the reference a pasted Sound reference to that Sound (ADR-0020), followed
  each millisecond. Pasted Sounds are Val, so such a Value needs the
  Val expression language, and it reaches only fields in the
  controller's own graph that take a control signal.

When the project's Virtual Control Surface has a control for the generated
Event Value, the Value maps from 0-1 to that control's minimum and maximum,
as a fader does. Without a control the Value passes unchanged.

A controller whose Value reads its own Event Value, directly or through
other controllers, is refused, as are two controllers generating the same
Event Value. A generated Event Value shadows any Event Value the project
supplies under that name. The controllers themselves produce no sound and
leave the compiled graph. A controller that is the project's only terminal
keeps recording its Value as timed events for the host.

Fields that hold lists of expressions in text, such as a
SyntheticSpectrumFromArray's Amplitudes or a Matrix's rows, are not
rewritten.

## Consequences

Generated Event Values behave alike offline and in realtime, at sample
accuracy for written Values and at the pasted Sounds' millisecond for
Sound-fed ones. A controller does not reach Sounds compiled separately,
such as another Live Set cell.
